naming_rules.rule: Latitude 4-digit code (2017+): 1st digit = series/tier: 3 = entry (3000), 5 = mainstream (5000), 7 = premium (7000), 9 = flagship (9000, introduced 2020).

3rd digit = model year (roughly tracks Intel gen): x8x = 2017 (7th gen), x9x = 2018 (8th gen Kaby Lake-R), x0x = 2019 (8th gen Whiskey Lake), x1x = 2020 (10th gen), x2x = 2021 (11th gen), x3x = 2022 (12th gen), x4x = 2023 (13th gen), x5x = 2024 (Core Ultra). Verified on 7480 (on sale Dec 2016, CES 2017), 7490 (Jan 2018), 7400 (May 2019), 7410 (May 2020), 7420 (CES 2021), 7430 (Apr 2022), 7440 (Mar 2023), 7450 (Mar 2024).

4th digit: 0 = standard model; 1 = higher-performance sibling (H-series CPU and/or dGPU, e.g. 5491/5591 Coffee Lake-H, 5401/5501 9th-gen H, 5411/5511, 5421/5521, 5431/5531 P-series); 5 = AMD Ryzen version (e.g. 5495, 7455).
1-suffix examples: Latitude 5491/5591 = 8th-gen Core H + optional MX130 (vs 5490/5590 = 15W U-series).

2-in-1 / Detachable / Ultralight are words after the number, not digits (e.g. '7410 2-in-1', '9420 2-in-1', '7350 Detachable', '7330 Ultralight'). Same number can be clamshell or convertible with different RAM (2-in-1 often soldered LPDDR), battery and weight; 9410 and 9440 were sold only as 2-in-1.

'E' prefix was used up to the 2016 models (E7470, E5470) and dropped from 2017 (7480). So E7450 (2015, 5th-gen Broadwell) is NOT 7450 (2024, Core Ultra); likewise E7440/E5440 (2014) vs 7440/5440 (2023). Vietnamese shops often still write 'E7420/E7410' for the newer models - go by CPU, not the prefix.

5x9x vs 5x0x: both carry 8th-gen Core, but 5490/5590 (2018) use Kaby Lake-R (i5-8250U/8350U, i7-8650U) while 5400/5500 (2019) use Whiskey Lake (i5-8265U/8365U, i7-8665U). Same for 7490 vs 7400. Check the CPU suffix 50U vs 65U.

Exception (3000 series): codes were reused. Latitude 3440/3540 (2013-14, 4th-gen Haswell, no E prefix) differ from 3440/3540 (2023, 12th/13th gen). Same risk for 3x50/3x60. Always confirm by CPU generation.

Vostro (2016+ scheme): 1st digit = series (3 = entry, 5 = mainstream), 2nd = screen size (3 = 13in, 4 = 14in, 5 = 15.6in, 6 = 16in), 3rd = generation/year (0 = 2020: 3400/3500; 1 = 2021: 3510/5410/5510; 2 = 2022: 3520/5620; 3 = 2023: 3530/5630; 4 = 2024: 5640). Older decoder: '1st number series generation, 2nd display size, 3rd processor generation'.
Vostro last digit: 0 = Intel, 5 = AMD Ryzen sibling on the same chassis (5410 Intel i5-11300H/i7-11370H vs 5415 Ryzen 5 5500U; 5515 Ryzen 5000U; 5625/5635 16in AMD; 3405/3425/3515 AMD).
Vostro 5415/5515 look nearly identical to Intel 5410/5510; only the CPU platform differs (Ryzen 3 5300U/5 5500U/7 5700U).
Vostro last digit 2 = mid-cycle 2020 Tiger Lake models (Vostro 14 5402, 15 5502); they precede 5410/5510 (2021, Tiger Lake H35).

Vostro exception: names 3400 and 3500 were also used in 2010 (1st-gen Core i3/i5/i7 Arrandale) - a '3400' listing with a 1st-gen CPU is the old model. Vostro line ended in 2024 (merged into Inspiron, then the 'Dell' brand).

January 2025 Dell brand unification: Dell (formerly XPS, Inspiron, Vostro), Dell Pro (formerly Latitude and OptiPlex), Dell Pro Max (formerly Precision); tiers Base / Plus / Premium (not all tiers in every line).
Dell Pro = formerly Latitude & OptiPlex; Dell = formerly XPS, Inspiron and Vostro.

Dell Pro tiers map roughly to old Latitude series: Base (plain 'Dell Pro 14') ~ 3000, Plus ~ 5000, Premium ~ 7000. Dell's own examples: Latitude 3450 -> Dell Pro 14, Latitude 5350 -> Dell Pro 13 Plus, Latitude 7350 -> Dell Pro 13 Premium. A lower 'Dell Pro 14 Essential' (PV14250/PV14255) also exists.

Dell model identifier has 5 elements (Dell doc): product line category + tier/configuration + form factor/screen size + generation (launch calendar year) + CPU vendor/differentiator. Dell's example: 'P A 13 250' = Dell Pro 13 Premium.

Decoding PA14250 / PB14250 / PC14250: P = Dell Pro line; A = Premium, B = Plus, C = Base (V = Essential); 14 = 14in (16 = 16in); 25 = 2025 launch year; last digit 0 = Intel, 5 = AMD. Examples: PA14250 = Pro 14 Premium (Intel), PB14250 = Pro 14 Plus (Intel), PC14250 = Pro 14 (Intel), PC14255 = Pro 14 with Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350, PV14255 = Pro 14 Essential with Ryzen 5 220. Letter-to-tier mapping is inferred from Dell product listings; Dell's doc shows only the PA13250 example.
AMD Dell Pro example on Dell.com: 'Dell Pro 14 Plus Laptop PB14255' (Ryzen).
